'''The Roil''' was a large, near-[[Navigator/Legends|unnavigable]] [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]] located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Gordian Reach/Legends|Gordian Reach]] [[Sector/Legends|sector]]. It consisted of [[Color/Legends|multicolored]] dust and [[Gas/Legends|gas]] clouds and contained several young [[Star/Legends|stars]]. The Roil separated the [[Loop Worlds]] and [[Back Reach]] areas of the Gordian Reach, and the [[Korphir Trace]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] passing through it was the only connection between the two regions. Nevertheless, for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] [[Privateer/Legends|privateers]] from the [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Korphir]] used secret [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] routes through the nebula.

==Description==
The large [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]] known as the Roil was located in the [[Gordian Reach/Legends|Gordian Reach]] [[Sector/Legends|sector]], a part of the [[Trans-Hydian/Legends|Trans-Hydian]] portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. It was situated between the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] known as the [[Junction-Tierell Loop/Legends|Junction-Tierell Loop]] and the [[Wetyin's Way]] [[spinward]] and the [[Ardan Cross]] and the [[Feena Run]] in the [[trailing]] direction. Southward, the vast cloud extended to the [[Maridun system/Legends|Maridun system]]. The nebula served as a dividing line between the [[Loop Worlds]] and [[Back Reach]] areas of its sector.<ref name="TEA" />

The Roil consisted of garish, many-[[Color/Legends|colored]] dust and [[Gas/Legends|gas]]. The [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Arkuda]] in the nearby [[Arkuda system/Legends|Arkuda system]] was known for its spectacular [[Local day/Legends|nighttime]] [[Atmosphere/Legends|skies]], and [[the Cometwash]], a [[Blue giant/Legends|blue giant]]&ndash;type [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] by swarms of [[Comet/Legends|comets]] in the [[Star system/Legends|star system]] of the [[The Cometwash system/Legends|same name]] that was located at the Roil's edge, was likewise famous for the sights it offered to visitors.<ref name="TEA" />

A stellar nursery, the Roil contained clumps of young blue and white stars. The fringes of the nebula were also the site of the knot of [[Protostar/Legends|proto-stars]] known as the [[Vallusk Cluster/Legends|Vallusk Cluster]]. It was nearly impossible for [[Starship/Legends|starships]] to [[Navigator/Legends|navigate]] through the Roil; an exception was the [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] route known as the [[Korphir Trace]], which passed through the nebula at its southern section and connected the Arkuda and [[Korphir system/Legends|Korphir systems]], serving as the only connection between the Loop Worlds and the Back Reach.<ref name="TEA" />

==History==
For [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] prior to the end of the existence of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], which [[Declaration of a New Order|transformed]] into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the natural barrier posed by the Roil was exploited by [[Privateer/Legends|privateers]] from the world [[Korphir]], who preyed upon shipping along the Junction-Tierell Loop before returning to Korphir via secret routes through the nebula.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|This map elicited a complaint from Modi about my insistence on putting nebulae everywhere. Sorry man.|Jason Fry, on ''The Essential Atlas'' map of the Gordian Reach|<ref name="Blog">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2009/08/endnotes-for-star-wars-essential-atlas_31.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 5 of 5)}}</ref>}}
The Roil was introduced in the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', authored by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]], which placed it in grid squares Q-5 and Q-6.<ref name="TEA" /> Beside the Roil, the map of ''The Essential Atlas'' illustrating the Gordian Reach also depicted the [[Denarii Nebula/Legends|Denarii Nebula]], and Fry later noted that, when creating that map, the book's chief cartographic illustrator, [[Modi]], had complained about Fry's insistence that all maps of the work feature nebulae.<ref name="Blog" />
